arguments.root_cause_statement: The Service search in namespace search selects pods with .spec.selector {app: search-api}, but the only pods that back the search backend are produced by Deployment search, whose pod template labels are {app: search}. No pod in the namespace carries app=search-api, so the endpoint controller populates no addresses for the Service and its Endpoints object has no subsets. The two search pods are Running, Ready and logging "search: serving on :8080", so the backend itself is healthy; traffic simply never reaches it, and the web-gateway pod logs a continuous stream of "gateway: search fetch FAILED (timeout or connection refused)", which is the storewide search timeout the page describes. Fixing it is a one-field edit: set the Service selector to app=search so it matches the Deployment's pod template labels.
arguments.mechanism: The Service search in namespace search has .spec.selector set to {app: "search-api"} while the pods that should back it are labelled {app: "search"}; the selector matches nothing, so the endpoint controller writes an Endpoints object search with no subsets and every connection to the Service's ClusterIP on port 8080 has no backend to be routed to.

evidence.claim: Service search has zero endpoint addresses while both search pods are Running and Ready
The Service's selector asks for app=search-api
The Deployment search labels its pods app=search, which cannot match app=search-api
The Endpoints object search contains no subsets/addresses
The web-gateway's calls to the search Service never complete
evidence.quote: gateway: search fetch FAILED (timeout or connection refused)

evidence.claim: The search backend itself is serving on port 8080

ruled_out.alternative: The search backend pods are themselves broken or not listening
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The search pod logs show the process bound to port 8080 and both pods report ready=True with zero restarts

ruled_out.alternative: The CrashLoopBackOff in namespace analytics-batch is the cause of the search outage
ruled_out.ruling_claim: That workload is a report-generator deployment in a different namespace with no Service or reference tying it to the search backend, so it cannot explain empty Endpoints for the search Service

ruled_out.alternative: The readiness probe on the search pods is failing, so ready pods are excluded from Endpoints
ruled_out.ruling_claim: Both search pods are reported ready=True, so readiness is not what is keeping addresses out of the Endpoints object
ruled_out.quote: pod/search-5478989674-6rxcp phase=Running labels={app=search, pod-template-hash=5478989674} node=incident-lab-control-plane api(ready=True,restarts=0)

verification.command: kubectl -n search get service search -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'
kubectl -n search get endpoints search -o yaml
